slides.title: Understanding Function Decorators
slides.prompt: A decorator is a callable that accepts a function as an argument and returns a new transformed function. The '@' syntax is syntactic sugar for wrapping and reassigning the function.

slides.title: Applying Decorators Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in the symbol used before a decorator name above a function definition.

slides.title: Syntactic Sugar Equivalence
slides.prompt: Which manual assignment is equivalent to using `@decorator` above `def my_func(): pass`?

slides.title: Handling Generic Function Arguments
slides.prompt: Fill in the missing keyword arguments parameter syntax inside a generic wrapper function.

slides.title: Decorator Execution Time
slides.prompt: When is a decorator function executed in Python?
options: At module import / function definition time
Only when the decorated function is explicitly called
Only when called inside a try-except block
slides.correctAnswer: At module import / function definition time

slides.title: Wrapper Return Statement
slides.prompt: Fill in the statement used by wrapper functions to deliver the target function's output.

slides.title: Multiple Decorators Stacking Order
slides.prompt: Given `@decA` placed above `@decB` on function `foo()`, in what order are decorators applied?
